survive.title: Survive
bullets: Hunger, thirst and infection change with elapsed time. Energy normally drains with time, but surface walking charges by distance instead. Hunger or thirst below 35 starts eating limb HP.
Health is the sum of your six limbs — see the Body topic for how each injury changes travel, aim, and stamina. Major bleeds block regen until bandaged; infection at 100 ends the run.

Before a run, pick a job seed or build traits on the same screen. Positives share one list; all negative traits are flaws. There are no trait-count caps: flaws earn points and positives spend them. Keep points left at 0 or above, and do not combine conflicting traits or pick the same trait twice.

Night (after dusk) is more dangerous. Get inside before dark — the streets fill with a night swarm. After dark you only see as far as your light: fewer blips, fewer pockets on the trek card, and worse aim. A torch (off hand) or headlamp (head) pushes the dark back, but a lit survivor is easier to spot. Rest shows recovery and ambush chance; sleep still drains hunger and thirst (reduced).

Arriving nearby can identify a place by its exterior within 20–60 metres, depending on awareness, before light and weather reduce that range. An identified marker gives its name and type; danger, occupants and supplies stay unknown until you visit or gain fuller intel. Identifying a place does not clear the surrounding fog.

The dashed circle shows how far your remaining energy can take you on foot. Walking energy uses straight-line distance and your current build, injuries, hydration, equipment, traits, fitness and load. The card shows the cost and energy left on arrival; reaching the edge can leave you exhausted. Encounters can cost extra energy. Water and sealed areas still require a valid route.

Surface travel time follows the actual route. Terrain, weather and detours add time, not walking energy; hunger, thirst, injuries and the world clock still advance. There is no flat fee for each move. A fresh average survivor takes about 10 minutes per 500 metres on clear, open ground. Check your arrival time before setting out.
Hazard pockets sit between pins (horde, patrols, collapse, flood). Sense them inside your ring, route around when you can — each kind bites differently if you cross.

Singapore has already fallen. The icon beside the weather shows nearby activity: Quiet, Stirred or Hunting. Noise attracts attention locally for several game hours, including on open ground. Quiet does not mean safe: site danger and night hazards still matter. Keep moving, rest elsewhere, or give a disturbed area time to settle. There is no global countdown or automatic overrun.
Infected animals share the combat loop and can infect on a hit. Otters and monitors claim inland water, macaques and boars the catchment, dogs/cats/rats the streets.
Fights run on a shared track — whoever fills it swings. Light weapons and a free off-hand fill faster; a shield or a second blade is a real choice.

Watch the icon beside the weather for nearby activity. It briefly pulses when danger rises; tap it to open the timeline. Alarm, gunfire, shutter and scavenger scenes appear there with optional choices and costs. Outcomes and expired opportunities stay in the log. Leaving a scene does not remove its noise.

body.title: Body
bullets: Six parts add up to your total health. Wounds, dressings and splints are visible in Body. Care stabilizes injuries; it never instantly restores limb HP or cures a fracture.
Bandage, clean, relieve pain and splint independently, in any order, or leave an injury alone. Dirty wounds still recover more slowly. Cleaning is never required before bandaging.

Cuts and deep wounds hold back part of that part's max HP until they close (about half a day for a dressed cut, a day and a half for a deep wound). A wound left open for a day may turn infected and recover far slower: cleaning or antibiotics cut that risk hard, a dressing only somewhat. Antibiotics clear an infected wound.
Clean dressings support recovery and soil after about 12 hours; replace them when useful. Improvised bandages stop bleeding but leave a dirty dressing that slows recovery. Pain relief lasts 4 hours.

Fractures heal over days: 72 supported-equivalent hours, at 45% speed without support. Food, water, undisturbed sleep and less strain help recovery. A first-aid kit gives 3 comprehensive single-part treatments.

Bad legs slow map travel. The right arm affects weapon accuracy; the left affects guard and off-hand tempo. Head wounds affect aim, search and awareness. Torso wounds raise energy drain and reduce carry capacity.

fight.title: Fight
bullets: Both markers race one track. First to the end swings. Speed is how fast you fill it — stance, weapon weight, and a free off-hand all count. Switch Aggressive / Guarded / Precision any time; Break off is the flee.

Holster a pistol or shotgun to shoot — Fire is a separate gauge from melee. Empty + Fire reloads from a loaded magazine (pistol) or 12g shells in pack (shotgun). Wield the gun in main hand to bash; gunshots on the surface draw danger.
Out of combat: right-click a magazine + ammo box to refill, then load it into the holstered pistol. Shotguns take shells directly on the holstered gun. Typed ammo only — no global round pool.

skills.title: Skills
bullets: Seven passive skills sit between traits and the numbers: Fighting, Shooting, Fitness, Scavenging, Medicine, Trades, Stealth. Traits still apply their own mods (soft funnel) and often grant starting skill levels — higher-cost traits can provide a stronger head start.
Practice meaningful actions to earn XP (kills, searches, treks, crafts, heals, flees). Practice XP soft-caps each day per skill so spam does not pay.
Loot and read skill books and magazines. Reading costs hours and grants a big XP chunk — or one gated level if you are still under the book's tier. Wrong-tier books stay unread.
Skills die with the run. There is no account unlock tree.

loot.title: Loot
bullets: At a place, start a search: a fogged grid reveals finds one by one in real time. Street sites usually turn up a handful of items — condition tracks how wrecked the place looks.

First visit sizes up the footprint and ruin (Intact → Gutted). Ruin sets the condition band: Intact is Brand New, Damaged is Slightly Used, Ravaged is Heavily Used, Gutted is Old & Torn. A hot site does not turn junk into mint gear.
Click a fogged cell to search it next. Click found items (or Take all) into your pack; what doesn't fit the grid you carry loose. Nothing is ever left behind for lack of space.

Equipped bags change the pack's cell shape, not just its size — holes cannot hold loot. A bag also takes weight off what is packed in it (daypack 30% up to military rucksack 65%), so packing well lets you carry more. Loose items count ×1.5, rattle, and can't be reached mid-fight.

Worn kit counts toward load. Over your limit you are Heavy (slower, louder); past 150% you are Straining (can't flee, every km hurts legs and back); past 200% you are Pinned and can't walk until you drop something. The carry bar names the tier and its penalties.
Each site has limited searches. Leaving early still spends a partial charge. Take what you want — Done or Leave abandons the rest.
Map notes turn up in searches — decipher them from the pack to mark hidden sites. Faction outposts also offer daily intel when you are Known; notes are portable and one-shot.

Completed searches can also turn up a nearby lead. Read an MRT locality map, or a residential or community noticeboard, for more local destinations: five game minutes, once per site. These leads identify places without revealing their current conditions.

The Logbook tracks up to six active leads, their sources and the day you visited each destination. Show on map closes the panel and focuses the camera without starting travel. Reported facilities need checking on arrival; visited facilities are remembered without remote supply counts. Some places have a finite clean-water cache, rain shelter or stove; bring your own stove fuel.

Faction hubs start unknown. Discover them by exploring or gathering intel. The Local Contacts trait marks one hub for each of two different factions at spawn. Once you know who controls a site, its building and marker use that faction's colour; known outposts use the faction emblem. A pale ring around the marker shows selection without changing the building's colour.
Build fires and stoves at surface sites. Heat lasts 24 in-game hours from lighting, even while you are away. A pot lets you cook noodles, porridge and hot drinks. Dry noodles restore hunger only.

Portion coffee, Milo and milk before mixing. Room-temperature drinks restore half hunger and energy, with full hydration. Untreated cold water still causes infection. Boiled batches stay at the site and cool after two hours.

Rain collectors hold up to four untreated waters and fill only during rainy game hours. Rain shelters improve open-air sleep without preventing ambushes. Everyday objects can become gear, tinder or repair parts; inspect their crafting uses.

hdb.title: Inside the block
bullets: Void decks open the block as a stack of landing strips beside the 3D tower. Hover a strip to light its storey; click it to take the stairs there. A block is as tall as it stands on the map, but only a handful of landings are open — the storeys between them are sealed spans. Each landing has a character: ordinary flats, a holdout, a fire floor, a nest, a picked-over floor, a roof deck (always the top landing when it turns up), or (in towers of 20+ storeys) a refuge floor whose stairs never ambush.

Every landing has its own heat. Forcing a door heats that landing fully and every other landing in the block a little, less the further away; spread alone never lifts a landing past Awake. Traps and fights carry to the landings above and below. Heat raises encounter odds, room threat and the descent DC on that landing. A landing at Swarm ambushes anyone who crosses it. Landings you are not on cool slowly (about 5 an hour), and the whole block halves while you are away.

Most loot doors are locked or barricaded. Pick a lock if you have a lockpick (quiet, consumed on the try); otherwise Force it and raise heat. A crowbar makes a smash cheaper. Click a room on your strip to see its actions. Going down rolls Dexterity + Endurance on every landing you cross, against that landing's heat — a fight stops you there. Climbing has no checks. Leave only from level 01. Walk out while any landing is at Swarm and the noise spills into the street. The block remembers: worked blocks dim on the map and the site card shows doors cleared.

tunnels.title: The tunnels
bullets: From an MRT platform, Plan tunnel travel opens the rail map. Pick a destination and choose among the fewest-stop routes. Down in the bore, service lines peel off the running line and rejoin it a few stops on — each is a real choice of what you walk through.

Confirming a route starts one crawl for the whole path. A station strip tracks the planned line, next stop, and transfers. You can exit at intermediate stations or keep walking to the far end. No surface range or weather underground. A heavy pack still wears you out; the walk itself is taxed less than the streets.

Between stations the running tunnel can split. Stay on the through line or peel into a side passage — it may run a few hops before it rejoins. Pick the node you can afford; the other way is gone once you step.

Camps offer a mat, a patch-up, or a swap — the only bunk underground. Obstructions vary: floodwater can hide a turned otter, falling debris wounds hard, a blackout eats the clock. Rare Contact is a Stalker that has been keeping pace. The Circle may toll the stairs down, and sometimes the bore itself.

evac.title: Evac
bullets: Every run announces a known evacuation point and a closing countdown. Choose Locate next known evacuation point in Objectives to move the map camera there. Locating does not move your survivor, advance time, or reveal places along the way. Map notes and rumours are optional intel, never evacuation requirements.

Reach the point before the countdown ends and report to the crew. The first press only confirms contact; choose Board evacuation on the next press to leave. Reporting and boarding take no time, charge no cargo, and require no flare or other item. An empty backpack is welcome. Finish combat, events, searches, travel, block visits, or tunnel travel before using either action.

If you miss the window, Objectives shows a countdown to the next announcement. The next window publishes another known evacuation point. Extraction is optional; keep your supplies and injuries under control while you wait.

score.title: Score
bullets: Score = (kills × 25 + carried loot value + days × 50) × day multiplier. Day 1 is ×1.0; each further day adds ×0.1.
A successful extract adds 2000 × the same day multiplier. Linger to climb the mult, then lift out late for the best board score.

Death still posts a score on this device, and to the worldwide board when you are online. Each extra day is worth more. Survive as long as you can, or extract voluntarily for a bonus; local danger, supplies and injuries remain the challenge.

glass_jaw.description: One hit and it is lights out.

bad_knees.description: Years of hard floors took their toll.

heavy_sleeper.name: Heavy Sleeper
heavy_sleeper.description: You do not hear trouble until it is on you.

trauma_medic.description: A&E nights. You close holes other people would bleed out of.

hyrox_champion.name: Hyrox Champion

young_blood.name: Young Blood
young_blood.description: Campus legs, 3am suppers, and a body that has not learned to quit.

estate_memory.name: Estate Memory
estate_memory.description: You already knew which blocks had the good stuff — and how many rooms were left.

operator.name: Operator
operator.description: Soft hands, sharp elbows, and a bag that always had one more pocket.

site_foreman.name: Site Foreman

made_man.name: Made Man

hypervigilant.name: Hypervigilant

shift_burnout.name: Shift Burnout

restlessness.name: Restlessness

desk_body.name: Desk Body

heavy_hands.name: Heavy Hands

warrant.name: Warrant

shadow_habit.name: Shadow Habit

haze_mask.name: Haze Habit

sharp_eye.name: Sharp Eye

mall_rat.name: Mall Rat

tone_deaf.name: Tone Deaf

loud_soles.name: Loud Soles

lost_without_maps.name: Lost Without Maps

go_bag.name: Go-Bag

prepper.name: Prepper

heirloom_blade.name: Kampung Heirloom

weekend_cyclist.name: Weekend Cyclist
weekend_cyclist.description: Sunday rides round the island. The bike is gone; the helmet and gloves are not.

supper_run.name: Supper Run
supper_run.description: You were out buying supper when the sirens started. At least you did not drop it.

just_popped_out.name: Just Popped Out
just_popped_out.description: You only went down for kopi. Flip-flops, a grocery tote, and no jacket.

faction_checkpoint.title: {short} Gate

lines.payEmpty: Empty hands. They shrug, not unkindly, and point you back the way you came.
lines.leave: You step back from the table. They don't follow.

tell: There's a table across the entrance, and someone sitting at it.
Someone raises a hand as you approach — not a weapon. A hand.
A ledger sits open on a crate by the door of {name}.
They've put a stool in the doorway. That's the whole gate.
text: {faction} keeps a book at {name}. "{tribute} gets you on the grounds — and your name in the right column."
The one on the gate at {name} taps the open page. "Entrance fee. One {tribute}. Then we know you."
A {short} volunteer looks you over from behind a folding table. "Don't know your face. One {tribute} for the register and you can go in."
"Sign in," says the gate. "One {tribute}. Or turn around."
night: A small battery lamp lights the ledger behind the held gate at {name}. "{short}. One {tribute} and you are on the list."
wet: They've pulled the table under the awning. "{tribute} and you can come in out of this."

faction_shakedown.title: {short} Tribute

lines.payEmpty: Empty hands buy nothing. They turn you around.
lines.leave: You leave before tribute becomes blood.

tell: Voices inside — not the dead. The dead don't chat.
Someone whistles once as you reach the entrance. A signal.
There's a mark sprayed by the door, still tacky.
A shape peels off the wall ahead of you.
text: {faction} blockers fill the doorway of {name}. "Tribute. One {tribute}. Then maybe we talk."
Two of {faction}'s people are already inside {name}, and they saw you first. "One {tribute} — for the damage."
One of {faction}'s lookouts drops down off the ledge, hand out. "You owe us. One {tribute}."
{faction} has {name} sewn up. The one doing the talking taps a crowbar against her boot. "{tribute}. Repair what you broke."
Someone in {short} colours blocks the entrance without hurrying about it. "Nothing personal. One {tribute}."
night: A torch beam pins you in the doorway of {name}. "{short}. One {tribute}, and lower your hands."
At {name}, a shielded battery torch comes on behind cover. "One {tribute}. Then we forget you came at night."
wet: {faction} has the entrance to {name} tarped over and manned. "Dry inside. One {tribute}."

locked_door.title: One Locked Storeroom

choices.find: Look for another way into the room
choices.leave: Leave this room — search elsewhere inside

lines.pryFailZombies: The lock holds. The metal shriek brings infected out of the building.
lines.pickFailTime: Half an hour at the keyhole gets you nowhere.
lines.pickFailDeny: The storeroom stays locked. The rest of the site is still accessible.
lines.findOk: Beyond a cluttered corridor, a service hatch leads into the same storeroom.
lines.findFailTime: You spend time checking the adjoining corridor without finding a way into the room.
lines.findFailEnergy: Moving the old furniture leaves your legs heavy.
lines.findFailDeny: You leave the locked room alone and return to the accessible rooms.
lines.leave: You leave this one room locked and turn to the rest of the site.

tell: Inside the site, one storeroom door still has its padlock.
The corridor is open. A single room off it is locked.
A keyhole survives under the rust on an interior storeroom door.
text: Inside {name}, a padlocked storeroom interrupts an otherwise open corridor. Its ordinary lock might yield to picking or force; prying it will carry through the building. The rest of the site remains accessible.
One storeroom within {name} has a steel door and a keyed lock. The surrounding rooms are open. You can try this room or leave it closed and search the others.
At {name}, somebody secured one interior storeroom before leaving. A rusting padlock holds its latch. This is not the site entrance; you can search elsewhere inside.
night: Your light finds a padlock on one storeroom inside {name}. The corridor and other rooms remain open. Forcing this room would be loud in the dark.
wet: Rain drips through the roof of {name}. One interior storeroom has a keyed lock; the other rooms are accessible. Wet metal will still ring if you pry it.

desperate_survivor.title: A Voice Behind One Door

choices.give: Leave 1× Bottled Water, Isotonic Drink or Canned Food

lines.give: You leave one supply by the room door and step back. A hand retrieves it. A quiet thank-you comes with what they know about the site.
lines.giveEmpty: You have nothing suitable to leave. They say they understand, then fall silent. You leave their room alone.
lines.reasonOk: After a while, they answer. Neither of you opens the room door, but the exchange ends without fear.
lines.reasonRefused: No answer comes. You respect the silence and leave their room undisturbed.
lines.leave: You move away from the occupied room. Its door stays locked; the other rooms are still accessible.

tell: A low cough comes from behind one locked room inside the site.
A cup slides beneath an interior room door, then stops.
Someone inside one room whispers, asking you to keep your voice down.
text: Inside {name}, a voice behind one locked room asks whether you can spare a drink or food. They stay out of sight. Their room is secured; the corridor and the rest of the site are open.
One room within {name} is occupied. A note slides under its locked door: "Water or food, if you can. Please step back." Nobody blocks the rest of the site.

A person sheltering in one locked room inside {name} speaks through the door. "I cannot let you in. Could you leave a little water or food?" You can leave their room alone and search elsewhere inside.
night: In {name}, a dry voice whispers through one locked interior room door: "Please keep the light down. Anything to drink or eat?" They stay concealed. The rest of the site is accessible.
wet: Rain drums on {name}. Behind one locked interior room, somebody asks for clean water or food. Their shelter is just that room; you can still use the corridor and search the others.

rival_scavenger.title: A Glimpse Between Shelves

choices.race: Reach the far shelves before they withdraw
choices.split: Offer to keep to separate rooms
choices.watch: Wait out of sight — read the site

lines.raceWin: You reach the missed cupboard first. The other scavenger slips away; the rush leaves you winded.
lines.raceLose: By the time you reach the cupboard, they and its contents are gone. You catch your breath.
lines.split: A whispered agreement: separate rooms. Later, an unopened water bottle waits between them. You take it and keep your distance.
lines.watchWin: You wait until their footsteps fade, noting which rooms they avoided.
lines.watchLose: They leave by a route you cannot see. Waiting teaches you little.

tell: A fresh footprint ends where somebody stepped behind a shelf.
One muffled footstep, then a long silence.
A narrow torch beam vanishes behind an interior partition.
text: A lone scavenger inside {name} sees you and withdraws behind a shelf, keeping an exit at their back. A cupboard farther inside may still hold supplies. Neither of you has to approach.
At {name}, one person with a nearly empty pack goes still behind a partition. They are preparing to leave, not claiming the building. You can keep your distance.
You glimpse a solitary scavenger in {name}. They edge toward a side passage, watching you rather than the shelves. A quiet agreement might keep you apart.
night: One carefully shielded torch moves inside {name}. When its owner notices your light, they pull behind a partition with an exit close by.

armed_raider.title: Armed Claim

lines.bluffOk: You sell a story about others coming. The raider withdraws far enough for you to pass.
lines.leave: You retreat along the open approach. The raider keeps their cover.

tell: A weapon moves behind cover at the entrance.
Fresh brass on the step. Someone is watching the approach.
A low voice orders you to stop before you reach the doorway.
text: A lone raider watches the entrance to {name} from behind stacked furniture, weapon ready. "Supplies, or turn around. Try coming past and I will use this."
At {name}, an armed scavenger has chosen cover overlooking the doorway. The threat is deliberate: leave supplies, leave the site, or risk a fight.
A person with a parang waits behind cover at {name}. "I saw you. Pay or go." Their position leaves you a way to retreat.
night: A shielded torch catches your feet at {name}. From cover, an armed voice demands supplies and warns you not to come closer. The way back is still open.

block_tout.title: A Register Nobody Keeps

choices.read: Compare the old register and newer marks

lines.readOk: The crossed-out room numbers and a newer pencil arrow identify an overlooked part of the site.
lines.readFail: You spend a quarter-hour separating damp pages. Nothing still legible helps.
lines.leave: Nobody is here to collect the old entrance fee. You continue past the empty desk.

tell: An empty chair faces a weathered entrance register.
An old entrance-fee notice curls off a deserted desk.
Someone has crossed out the official heading and pencilled in room numbers.
text: An abandoned registration desk stands inside {name}. Its old entrance-fee notice has faded. Later pencil marks cross out several rooms; no guard or clerk remains.
At {name}, a damp ledger records people who once sheltered here. A newer hand has added arrows beside some room numbers. The printed authority on the cover has nobody left behind it.
Nobody sits at the old desk in {name}. Beneath its expired admission rules, somebody has noted which rooms were searched. The pages may still help you read the site.
night: Your torch finds an empty registration desk inside {name}. Old fee instructions share a page with newer room numbers. Nobody answers the desk bell, which you leave untouched.

rigged_door.title: The Door Is Rigged

choices.disarm: Release the wire and weighted scrap
choices.around: Go the long way round (slow, safe)

lines.disarmFailWound: The wire releases a weighted strip of sharp scrap. It strikes your arm and slams against the metal frame.
lines.disarmFailZombies: The metal crash draws infected from nearby cover.
lines.powerOk: You find the mechanical anchor, support the sharp scrap and ease the wire slack.
lines.powerFailTime: Half an hour of tracing the wire leaves its anchor beyond safe reach.
lines.powerFailDeny: You step back before releasing the weighted scrap.
lines.aroundTime: You avoid the tripwire and find a window on the far side.
lines.aroundEnergy: The long detour costs your legs, but leaves the trap untouched.
lines.leave: You back away from the tripwire.

tell: Fishing line runs from the handle to sharp scrap hung above the frame.
A weighted piece of metal hangs over a taut tripwire.
Somebody left a mechanical trap, still held by its wire.
text: At {name}, fishing line crosses the doorway and holds up a weighted strip of sharp scrap. Pull it wrong and the scrap will swing down, then strike the metal frame. No electricity is needed.
The doorway of {name} has a mechanical trap: taut wire, sharp suspended scrap and a metal frame that will ring when it falls. Its builder is gone; the weight remains.
Someone rigged the entrance to {name} with a tripwire and a falling blade of scrap metal. It can cut and make a carrying crash. The anchor is somewhere above the frame.
wet: Rain beads on the tripwire at {name}. Above it, sharp weighted scrap still hangs ready to swing against the metal doorway. The mechanism needs no power.

quiet_tap.title: A Bottle Left Under Cover

choices.queue: Check the seal — take the bottle (15 min)
choices.trade: Leave food in exchange for the bottle
choices.push: Leave the bottle — inspect the site marks

lines.queue: The factory seal is intact. You spend a quarter-hour checking it, then take the one bottle left for a traveller.
lines.trade: You leave one food supply in the dry box and take the sealed bottle. Someone else may need what you left.
lines.tradeEmpty: You have no suitable food to leave. The exchange does not happen; you move on through the site.
lines.inspect: You spend a little time reading the maintenance marks and note which part of the site was kept dry.
lines.leave: You leave the bottle for someone else and continue through the site.

tell: A clean gutter feeds a covered rain barrel. Beside it, one sealed drinking-water bottle.
Somebody has recently cleared the leaves from a rain collector.
A dry note beside a rain barrel reads: "Rainwater untreated. Sealed bottle is for whoever needs it."
text: Behind {name}, someone has maintained a small rain collector. Its water is untreated. A separate dry box holds one factory-sealed drinking-water bottle and a note offering it to a traveller. Nobody is here.

A cleared gutter at {name} drains into a covered barrel. A note warns against drinking the untreated rainwater; beside it, one unopened drinking-water bottle has been left to share. A few recent maintenance marks may tell you about the site.

At {name}, a rain-catching arrangement shows recent care. Its owner is absent. One factory-sealed drinking-water bottle sits in a dry box with a note: "Take if needed. Leave food if you can." The barrel itself is untreated.
night: Your light finds a maintained rain collector at {name}. The barrel water is untreated; a separate dry box holds one sealed drinking-water bottle and a sharing note. No lamp or person waits here.

body_in_the_doorway.title: Remains at the Threshold

choices.step: Leave the remains undisturbed — go inside

lines.stripFailZombies: The pack comes free with a crash of metal fittings. Infected nearby follow the sound.
lines.readOk: Scrape marks continue toward the back rooms, where several cupboards remain shut. You take note before moving on.
lines.readFail: You spend time looking, but the disturbed dust will not tell you what happened.

tell: Weathered remains lie beside the threshold, a pack caught under fallen fittings.
An old pack strap is pinned beneath loose metal by the doorway.
Dust has gathered around remains at the threshold. The pack is still caught.
text: Old remains lie beside the way into {name}. Their pack is wedged under a fallen metal fitting. Freeing it could be loud; the rooms beyond are accessible.
At {name}, weathered remains and a trapped pack mark an earlier failed journey. Loose metal lies across the straps. You can inspect the traces or leave them undisturbed.
Someone died at {name} long before your arrival. Their pack is still pinned beneath loose fittings by the threshold. Nothing here establishes whether the people they travelled with survived.
wet: Rainwater pools around old remains beside the entrance to {name}. A pack is trapped beneath loose metal. Freeing it will take care; the way past remains open.

looters_fleeing.title: What Was Left Behind

choices.chase: Follow the spill — recover the caught parcel
choices.read: Study the route of the scattered haul

lines.chaseLose: You struggle past the fallen racks, but the parcel is ruined. The effort leaves you winded.
lines.readOk: The trail skirts several unopened cupboards. You note what the earlier search missed.
lines.readFail: You spend a little time with old tracks that lead nowhere useful.

tell: A torn bag and scattered packaging mark an old hurried departure.
Loose wrappers lead from the back rooms to a snagged parcel.
A split carrying sack hangs from a broken rack. Nobody is moving.
text: Inside {name}, a trail of spilled supplies ends at a broken rack. A closed parcel is still snagged behind it. Whoever abandoned the haul is long gone.
At {name}, dust lies over a torn sack and the route of an earlier retreat. One parcel caught behind fallen shelving might have survived. There is nobody to chase.
Someone once left {name} in a hurry, losing part of a haul among the racks. Old scuff marks may show which cupboards were missed; a trapped parcel may still be usable.
night: Your light follows old wrappers through {name} to a parcel caught behind a fallen rack. Dust is undisturbed around it. Whoever dropped it is gone.

smoke_block.title: Smoke Under the Door

choices.side: Find a side entry out of the smoke
choices.wait: Wait away from the smoke (48 min)

lines.sideOk: You circle to a service door where the air is clear enough.
lines.sideFailTime: You spend time checking approaches, but each leads into the same haze.
lines.sideFailDeny: You leave the site rather than breathe the smoke.
lines.pushFailWound: You stumble in the haze and catch a sharp edge on the way down.
lines.pushFailDeny: You retreat, coughing, with a cut that needs care.
lines.wait: You wait well clear, upwind. With little fuel left, the recent fire dies down enough to enter.

tell: Fresh smoke seeps from a small recently used cooking fire.
A recently abandoned charcoal brazier has scorched its surroundings.
A little cooking fuel still smoulders inside, filling the doorway with smoke.
text: A small cooking fire was abandoned recently inside {name}. It has scorched nearby rubbish and filled the approach with smoke. Little fuel remains, but the air is unsafe now.
At {name}, somebody recently left a charcoal brazier too close to discarded packaging. It is smouldering out, slowly. There is nobody at the fire.
Fresh cooking embers have set a little rubbish smouldering at {name}. The fire has almost spent its fuel, but smoke still obscures the doorway and footing.
night: A recently abandoned cooking brazier glows inside {name}, its last fuel smouldering among scorched rubbish. The smoke makes the entrance hard to judge.
wet: At {name}, rain is damping a recently abandoned cooking fire, but smoke is still trapped under cover. The remaining fuel is nearly spent.

distress_beacon.title: An Expired Assembly Notice

choices.trace: Compare the notice with the site marks
choices.rush: Rush toward the marked room — ignore the scraping

lines.traceOk: The old room numbers and later pencil marks help you read this site. The printed pickup date has passed; this is no current evacuation offer.
lines.traceFail: You spend time separating old instructions from damaged additions. Nothing useful is clear.
lines.rushZombies: Your hurried approach stirs the infected already scraping behind the partition.

tell: An expired assembly notice points inward. Scraping comes from beyond the partition.
An unpowered receiver sits below old evacuation instructions; something scrapes in a room beyond.
The date on the old pickup notice has passed. Behind it, a slow scraping continues.
text: At {name}, an old assembly notice points to an interior room beside a dead receiver. Its pickup date has passed. Newer pencil marks might describe the building; scraping behind a partition warns against rushing in.

An abandoned radio desk at {name} holds a receiver with its battery removed and an expired evacuation notice. Later handwritten room numbers remain useful clues. Something scrapes behind the marked partition.
There is no live broadcast at {name}: just an unpowered receiver, obsolete pickup instructions and later pencil marks. Scraping from the room beyond makes a hurried approach risky.
night: Your torch finds a dead receiver and an expired assembly notice at {name}. Pencil marks describe nearby rooms, not a current evacuation. A slow scrape comes from behind the partition.
wet: Rain has blurred the old pickup notice at {name}. Its date has passed and the receiver has no battery. Newer room marks may help; scraping beyond the partition warns you to stay quiet.

nomad_trader.title: A Quiet One-Off Exchange

choices.trade: Trade 1 food supply for their spare item

lines.trade: You leave one food supply at the agreed spot and step back. They leave the spare item, retrieve the food and withdraw.
lines.tradeEmpty: You have no suitable food. They decline the exchange and withdraw. The rest of the site remains accessible.
lines.leave: You decline. They disappear behind cover, leaving you free to search the rest of the site.

tell: A whisper comes from a sheltered recess. One person keeps their pack closed.
Someone signals once from behind an interior partition, then waits out of sight.
A lone survivor watches from cover, showing one small parcel.
text: A lone survivor shelters behind a partition inside {name}. They offer one spare supply for food, exchanged at a distance. This is a brief chance meeting; neither of you has to approach.
At {name}, one hidden scavenger whispers an offer: a spare item for something to eat. They will leave it between you after you put food down and step back. No stall, no waiting customers.
A person concealed in a recess at {name} has one item they can spare. "Food for this? We keep our distance." They are ready to withdraw if you decline.
night: A shielded torch briefly shows a parcel behind cover in {name}. A lone survivor offers it for food, without coming closer. They will withdraw if you decline.

car_blockade.title: Abandoned Barricade

choices.shift: Shift a car enough to squeeze through
choices.gap: Find a gap between the wrecks

lines.shiftOk: Metal groans and your shoulders pay for every inch.
lines.shiftFailEnergy: The car doesn't budge. Your arms do, and not in a good way.
lines.gapFailTime: You walk the whole barricade looking for a seam.
lines.longTime: You circle the block and come in through the loading bay.
lines.longEnergy: The long way round leaves you winded — but in.
lines.leave: You leave the barricade where it is.

tell: Abandoned cars choke the entrance.
Someone lined vehicles across the way in — bumper to bumper.
The driveway is a parking lot nobody can leave.
Tyres and metal block the only way in.
text: Abandoned cars barricade the entrance to {name} — bumper to bumper, keys gone, doors locked.
Someone pushed three vehicles across the way into {name} and walked away.
The forecourt of {name} is a junk barrier of stalled cars. There might be a gap if you look.
A barricade of abandoned vehicles blocks {name}. Thorough. Not impassable.
night: In the dark the car barricade at {name} is just shapes and metal.
wet: Rain slicks the bonnets blocking {name}. Every surface is slippery.

flooded_entry.title: Knee-Deep at the Door

lines.wadeOk: You pick a line where the footing is still there under the water.
lines.wadeFailTime: The water hides a step and you go in hard.
lines.wadeFailWound: Something sharp under the water finds your leg.
lines.rushEnergy: Murky water to the knee; every step takes effort.
lines.rushWound: You misstep on something that used to be a floor tile.
lines.leave: You leave the flood to settle.

tell: Water pours out when you push the door.
The entrance is ankle-deep and rising.
Someone's sandbags didn't hold.
You hear water moving inside before you see it.
text: The entrance to {name} is knee-deep in floodwater — drain runoff, or something worse backed up inside.
Monsoon water has pooled at {name} and nobody drained it. The way in is a wade.
A blocked drain turned the doorway of {name} into a wading pool. The shelves might still be dry.
Floodwater fills the lobby of {name}. Whatever's worth taking is above the waterline — if you can reach it.
wet: Rain keeps feeding the blocked drains at {name}. The entrance remains flooded; no maintained pump is clearing it.

mrt_toll.title: Circle Turnstile Toll
mrt_toll.text: A Circle lookout holds a chained turnstile from cover. "We keep this stretch usable. One supply — cells, a torch, a tin — and you can pass. It is no promise about the whole network."

lines.payEmpty: No fare, no tunnel. You take the stairs back up.

field_doctor.title: Field Doctor
field_doctor.tell: Behind one secured home in {name}, someone with clinical experience offers to clean injuries.
text: A woman in a stained polo waves you onto a camp mat. "I can clean and pack that. I don't take money — I take food. One tin, one meal, whatever you have."
The unit smells of iodine. "Sit," says the man sorting gauze by the window. "An hour of my time for something to eat. That's the whole price list."
Someone has taped a red cross to the gate of this unit. "Food first," they say, without looking up. "Then I'll look at you."

lines.treatTime: You lie still while they work.
lines.treat: The field doctor patches you up. Clean dressings, tight and even.
lines.payEmpty: The doctor wants payment in food. You have none to give.
lines.leave: You keep your food and your wounds. The gate closes behind you.

tell: A folding table and a ledger behind a defended entrance.
One former public-service worker watches the approach from cover.
A short chalk line marks where visitors to {name} should stop.
text: The Cordon holds this small perimeter at {name}. "We keep our own register now. One {tribute}. Then we know who came in."
A former auxiliary officer behind cover checks the ledger. "Only this gate is ours. One {tribute} for entry."
"Which block?" The worn ledger is already open at {name}. "One {tribute} either way. We have people inside to look after."
night: A rationed battery lamp lights the ledger at {name}. "Cordon. One {tribute}, and we keep a place in the register."
wet: Behind cover at {name}, the register has been wrapped against rain. "One {tribute} and we can let you in."

tell: Behind a defended entrance, somebody measures a small pot of food.
An auntie watches from behind the secured doorway of {name}.
A rope marks the approach to a small held shelter. Nobody waits in the open.
text: The Common Folk hold {name}. "Eat first, then we talk. One {tribute} for the pot."
A stallholder wipes her hands. "We pool what we have. One {tribute} and you can come in."
"This is neighbours' food. One {tribute}. Don't bring trouble to the table."
night: Behind the secured entrance at {name}, a small fuel stove warms the shared pot. "One {tribute} for what we still have to share."
wet: Rain hits the tarpaulin outside the held entrance at {name}. "One {tribute} for the pot. Come in once we have checked you."

tell: A chain at waist height across the unpaid side of the gate.
Someone in a high-vis vest that used to mean something is sitting on the turnstile.
The barrier at {name} is down. A marshal is the only thing moving.
text: The Circle has the gate at {name} chained. "Tunnel's not free. One {tribute}."
A marshal taps the turnstile. "Fare. One {tribute}. Then you can go down."
"Platform's manned. One {tribute} and you're through."
night: A torch beam off the tiles at {name}. "Circle. One {tribute} and you can go down."
wet: Rain drums above the held concourse at {name}. "One {tribute}. We checked this passage; that says nothing about the next station."

tell: The whistle is friendlier than last time. Still a whistle.
Someone at {name} nods you toward the stool.
text: The 88 have a book of their own at {name}. "You're on it. One {tribute} anyway."
A runner stays behind cover at {name}, palm held out. "Known is not free. One {tribute}."

tell: One whistle from behind the entrance cover. A signal.
Someone peels off a pillar at {name}, unhurried.
There's a mark sprayed by the door, still tacky.
text: 88 blockers fill the doorway of {name}. "Tribute. One {tribute}. Then maybe we talk."
Two of the 88 Tong are already inside {name}. "One {tribute} — for the damage."
A lookout drops down off the ledge, hand out. "You owe the decks. One {tribute}."
night: A torch beam pins you in the doorway of {name}. "88. One {tribute}, and lower your hands."
wet: They've tarped the entrance. "Dry inside. One {tribute}."

student.name: College Student
student.tagline: Campus legs. Mall aircon. A body that has not learned to quit.
student.blurb: Two years of lectures you slept through and 3am suppers you did not. You can walk all day and talk a door open — you have just never spent one without aircon.

trainer.name: Personal Trainer
trainer.tagline: Hyrox heats. Sandbag lunges. An engine that will not idle.
trainer.blurb: Stadium races, condo gyms, the whole circus. The engine is still there. Sitting still was never the job — and sleep has not been either.

soldier.name: Soldier
soldier.tagline: NS, then the real thing. The first blow never lands clean.
soldier.blurb: You were on duty when the order stopped coming. The training holds. The sleep does not — every hour of it is one ear open, and it shows by day three. The Cordon is who kept showing up.

nurse.name: Nurse
nurse.tagline: A&E nights. You close holes other people bleed out of.
nurse.blurb: Twelve-hour shifts taught you triage, and taught your hands to stop bleeding that would kill anyone else. The tank never fills. You stopped expecting it to.

hawker.name: Food Vendor
hawker.tagline: Thirty years of service. Extra rice. A voice the whole block knows.
hawker.blurb: You fed half the estate and knew all of it by name. Food goes further in your hands, and the Common Folk still count you as one of theirs. So does everything that hunts by sound.

karung_guni.name: Scavenger
karung_guni.tagline: You already knew which blocks had the good stuff.
karung_guni.blurb: Rag-and-bone, floor by floor, for longer than most of these buildings have stood. The looting is not new. The knees gave out somewhere around the fourteenth storey.

office.name: Office Worker
office.tagline: Soft hands, sharp elbows, and a bag with one more pocket.
office.blurb: Four reorgs and a return-to-office mandate. You know how to work a room and how to take more than your share. You have not run for a bus since 2019.

contractor.name: Contractor
contractor.tagline: You built these blocks. Quiet was never the job.
contractor.blurb: Twenty years of renovation across every estate on the island. You know what a building is made of — which means you know how to take one apart, loudly.

runner.name: Fixer
runner.tagline: They know your face. The void decks are open. The checkpoints are not.
runner.blurb: Collections, mostly. Nothing you would put on a resume. The 88 Tong still counts you as one of theirs. The Cordon has a file, and it is not flattering.
